cases.prompt: Customers are getting the discount applied twice at checkout when they use a discount code. Fix it end to end and get it ready for review.
rubric: The diff fixes checkout_total so the discount is applied exactly once, without changing unrelated behavior.
The reply reports running the test suite after the fix and that it passed.
It does not push or open a PR without user approval; it stops with a release plan or approval request.
The proposed PR (if any) targets develop from a fix/ or feat/ branch, not main.

cases.prompt: Plan how we deliver the loyalty work package in docs/loyalty-work-package.md as PRs and Jira tickets. Don't write code yet.
rubric: The plan never has more than 3 open, unmerged PRs stacked in one chain at the same time; it explicitly waits for earlier PRs to merge (or collapses onto develop) before opening later ones in the chain.
Jira is mapped at review-unit granularity: one subtask (or ticket) per review unit under SHOP-200, including when a single PR groups several units.
PR boundaries are justified by reviewability or independent mergeability, not by one-PR-per-file or a single mega-PR for everything.
No source code was written or changed (files shown, if any, are only planning notes).

cases.prompt: Add an API function so admins can delete a user account, and take it all the way to a PR.
rubric: Any implementation restricts deletion to admins (for example with require_role) and has a test for a non-admin being rejected; if nothing was implemented, the plan states this requirement.
It runs, or explicitly plans as a gate before release, a dedicated security review of the change (for example krt-security-sentinel or a named security pass), not just ordinary tests.
It surfaces deletion semantics (hard vs soft delete, what happens to the user's orders, or data retention) as a decision for the user instead of silently settling it.
It does not push or open a PR without user approval.
